_README: Regression set for retrieval and answer quality. Run after any change to
search-term generation, tier filters, the quality floor, scoring, or the
library/live routing gate.
Run with: python eval/run_eval.py   (retrieval only - no LLM synthesis)
Fields per case:
id                 stable slug
question           exactly as a clinician would type it
mode               review | learn
force_route        live | library - PIN the retrieval path for this case
expect.route       the route the run must actually take
expect.min_papers  floor on evidence-base size
expect.min_sr      minimum Cochrane + Level I papers
expect.min_rct     minimum Level I papers
expect.min_terms           live only: search terms the generator produced
expect.min_hits_per_query  live only: mean PMIDs esearch returned per
query, from pubmed_audit.jsonl. Per-query, not total.
expect.max_empty_fraction  live only: max share of queries returning zero
expect.cochrane_papers_must_be_cochrane_journal  every cochrane-tier
paper's journal must be the Cochrane Database
context.exchanges  a Review thread this question is a follow-up IN.
Built into the prompt block with the app's own
build_context_block / context_prior_pmids.
expect.min_tiers_below_level1   tiers populated below level1. Case and
learn mode sweep every tier; review stops early.
expect.evidence_must_mention    term(s) that must appear in a retrieved
paper's title — how a follow-up's context is measured
on the EVIDENCE rather than on the prompt string.
expect.evidence_must_not_be_dominated_by   term(s) that must not appear
in a majority of retrieved titles (new-topic reset).
expect.clarify     case mode only: bounds on generate_case_followups —
count_between, must_not_ask_about,
every_question_states_its_reason. Costs one Haiku
call per case, the same order as the term generator.
why                what this case is guarding against
NOT YET ENFORCED by run_eval.py: must_contain, must_not_contain, banner,
modules_non_empty, max_unsourced_numeric_modules. These are ANSWER-level
assertions and the harness is retrieval-only, so they are recorded here as
intent and are inert until a synthesis mode exists. Do not read a passing
run as evidence that they hold.
ALWAYS SET force_route. A case without it measures whichever path the
library happens to favour that day, and write-back moves that line under
you: the laser case was written for a live search-term bug, then the fixed
run wrote 196 papers into the library and the same case silently began
testing the library path instead. A topic worth testing on both paths gets
two cases, one pinned each way.
ROUTES ARE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. eval/probe_routes.py runs each question
through the real coverage gate and reports where the measurement disagrees
with clinical expectation. Doing that surfaced the similarity-floor bug:
at the old 0.45 floor 18 of 20 questions routed to the library, including
'root canal treatment in pregnancy' with 63 hits above the floor and not
one on-topic paper among them. Floor raised to 0.55; split is now 12
library / 9 live. Where measurement is borderline, clinical judgement wins
and the case's why[] says so.

cases.question: Use of lasers in root canal disinfection
why: Retrieval regression, 2026-08-29. esearch returned 5 PMIDs across 28
queries because module search strings were bags of words that PubMed
ANDs together ('laser irradiation power settings endodontic
disinfection' matches 1 record in all of PubMed). Module 4 retrieved
zero papers and still emitted a numeric protocol - Er:YAG 20 mJ/15 Hz,
5.25% NaOCl 2 mL/60 s, ISO #30/.04 - invented and shipped behind a
disclaimer.
This topic is also a vocabulary trap: the literature lives under aPDT,
PIPS, SWEEPS, photodynamic therapy and Er:YAG, so any query that does
not OR-expand synonyms will miss it while appearing to succeed.
The first post-fix run reported 10 Cochrane reviews, which is not a
plausible number for this topic and was not real. COCHRANE_TERM was
'Cochrane Review[pt]', a publication type PubMed does not have; it was
translated to a word match on 'cochrane' ANDed with Review[pt], so any
SR that mentioned searching the Cochrane Library was promoted to the
top tier. Fixed to a journal-scoped filter. 109 library rows carrying
the false tag were demoted and rescored (median -7.8).
This case is PINNED to the live route. The bug was in live search-term
generation. The first fixed run wrote 196 papers back into the library,
so without the pin this question would serve from the library and the
term generator - the thing that actually broke - would never run. The
next '3-7 words' regression would pass the eval silently.
min_hits_per_query and max_empty_queries guard the real failure signal,
read from pubmed_audit.jsonl rather than from the evidence dict. The
visible symptom was a small evidence base, but the cause was esearch
itself returning almost nothing, and by the time papers reach the
evidence dict they have already passed the per-tier quality threshold -
a count taken there just shadows the paper count and says nothing about
whether the QUERY was broken. Measured from the audit log:
failing run  28 queries     5 hits   25 empty    0.2 hits/query
fixed run    28 queries   940 hits    0 empty   33.6 hits/query
eval run A   56 queries  2305 hits    7 empty   41.2 hits/query
eval run B    7 queries   205 hits    0 empty   29.3 hits/query
PER QUERY, not total. The term generator's output count varied with
parse luck - measured 5/10 Haiku responses were unparseable because
the model emits PubMed phrase quotes unescaped inside JSON strings,
and every failure silently fell back to ONE term. Fixed 2026-08-30:
line-based TERM: output contract, tolerant parser, corrective retry
(tests/test_search_term_parsing.py). Ten consecutive post-fix calls:
7 terms each. A total-hits threshold would still fail on term-count
variation, so the floor stays per-query.
max_empty is a FRACTION: niche angle-terms crossed with narrow tier
filters legitimately return zeros. The malformed-query signature is
MOST queries empty (25/28 = 89% in the regression), not some.
The harness reads these numbers from a shared audit log with no run
identity, so it skips esearch assertions when >10 terms appear in the
window (impossible from one run = concurrent retrieval interleaved).

baseline.note: Live route, retrieval only, via eval/run_eval.py after the Cochrane journal-scoping fix. Recorded as a RANGE over 4 consecutive runs, not a point: search terms are LLM-generated and the term count is not stable, so a point baseline would read as a regression on the next run. Thresholds are floors, set well below the observed range.
baseline.cochrane_note: 1 genuine Cochrane Database review in every run, down from the falsely-reported 10. This is the stable number and the one to watch.
baseline.variance_note: The 2x spread in paper count tracked term-count flapping (1 vs 3 with parse luck), fixed 2026-08-30 - see post_generator_fix.

post_generator_fix.note: First clean run after the term-generator fix (stable 7-8 terms). Papers roughly tripled vs the 1-term runs; expect future runs near this shape.

full_curriculum_reference.note: The 2026-08-29 17:29 run WITH synthesis, the only end-to-end cost measurement. run_eval.py does retrieval only and costs no LLM tokens.
full_curriculum_reference.cost_note: Four modules with real retrieval. Above the $0.50 target, and this is the honest number to quote. The failing 5-paper run cost $0.5968 - it met the target by not retrieving anything, so cost per run is not a quality metric.

regression_reference.note: The failing run, kept so the diff stays legible.

cases.question: Use of lasers in root canal disinfection
why: Companion to laser-root-canal-disinfection-live. Same question, other
path. The live case guards search-term generation; this one guards what
write-back actually deposited - if the 196 written-back papers were
mistiered or thinly embedded, this case degrades while the live case
stays green.
Pinned to library for the mirror-image reason the other is pinned to
live: without the pin, a library that lost coverage would silently fall
through to PubMed and the case would pass by measuring the wrong path.

baseline.note: Retrieval only, via scripts/probe_retrieval.py, after the Cochrane tier fix and the 109-row demotion.
baseline.cochrane_note: All three are genuine Cochrane Database reviews on adjacent topics, not laser-specific. That is the honest answer for a topic Cochrane has not reviewed.

cases.question: Single-visit versus multiple-visit root canal treatment for necrotic teeth with apical periodontitis
why: Draft said library and the topic is genuinely well covered (Cochrane CD005296 is in the library), but the measured gate at the 0.55 floor put it at 10 relevant hits - just under MIN_RAG_RELEVANT. Pinned library deliberately: this is THE canonical well-covered question, and if the library cannot answer it the library is the thing that is broken, which is what the case should surface.

PIN, 2026-08-30: the synthesis run for this case neither cited nor mentioned Cochrane CD005296 (PMID 36512807), the definitive review on exactly this question, present in the library at score 70.4. Root cause was not an over-narrow query but an embedding mismatch: the best-formed boolean scored it 0.546 (rank 11, cut by the 0.55 floor) while the raw question scored 0.680. A well-formed PubMed boolean is mostly operators and quotes, so it embeds further from prose than a sloppy one - the better the query, the worse the vector search. Fixed by union-KNN over the question plus every generated term (A4) and an authority guarantee (A5). must_include_pmid is checked on retrieval, must_cite_pmid on the generated answer.

cases.question: MTA versus Biodentine for full pulpotomy in mature permanent teeth with irreversible pulpitis
why: Measurement agrees with the draft: 36-60 relevant, 51+ high-tier. Among the best-covered topics in the library.

cases.question: Sodium hypochlorite concentration low versus high and outcome of primary root canal treatment
why: Measured 25 relevant. The literature genuinely conflicts here, so this case also guards the divided-literature banner.

cases.question: CBCT versus periapical radiography for detecting apical periodontitis
why: Measured 17 relevant, 12 above 0.60. Also guards that a diagnostic-accuracy question keeps its ALARA/selection-criteria caveat.

cases.question: Calcium silicate bioceramic sealers versus epoxy resin sealers outcomes
why: Measured 48-60 relevant, one of the densest topics. Short follow-up is the standing limitation.

cases.question: Nonsurgical retreatment versus apical microsurgery for persistent apical periodontitis
why: DISAGREES with the draft. At the 0.45 floor this looked like 89 relevant; at 0.55 it is 7, newest 2024. The apparent coverage was domain-vocabulary noise. Pinned live until the library genuinely holds the topic.

cases.question: Vital pulp therapy direct pulp capping in cariously exposed mature permanent teeth
why: Measured 50-55 relevant, 42 above 0.60. Position statements (ESE/AAE) are in the library as curated rows.

cases.question: Postoperative pain after root canal treatment preemptive NSAID versus placebo
why: Measured 34-38 relevant. A question where a cited effect direction is expected rather than a hedge.

cases.question: Regenerative endodontic procedures in immature necrotic teeth success and survival
why: Measured 26 relevant. This topic previously produced the apex-locator misretrieval that motivated the similarity floor, so it is worth a standing case.

cases.question: Cracked tooth prognosis after root canal treatment by crack extent
why: DISAGREES with the draft. 64 relevant at 0.45 collapsed to 10-11 at 0.55. Thin in this library; pinned live.

cases.question: Antimicrobial photodynamic therapy as an adjunct in primary molars with necrotic pulps
why: Measurement agrees: 8 relevant at 0.55. Paediatric aPDT is genuinely thin here.

cases.question: Endodontic management in patients on bisphosphonates or antiresorptives
why: Measurement agrees: 2-3 relevant. At the old 0.45 floor this showed 60 'relevant' hits that were entirely generic AAE position statements - the clearest single example of why the floor moved.

cases.question: Root canal treatment in pregnancy timing and local anesthetic choice
why: Pinned live against a borderline measurement (1 hit above 0.55 in the distribution sweep, 12 on a later run with different generated terms - it straddles MIN_RAG_RELEVANT). Hand-checked: not one on-topic paper in the library, the 'relevant' set was AAE position statements. Clinical judgement overrides the borderline number.

cases.question: Laser-activated irrigation PIPS SWEEPS versus ultrasonic activation periapical healing outcomes
why: DISAGREES with the draft. Measured 25-40 relevant - write-back from the laser runs genuinely populated this topic. Pinned library to guard what write-back deposited.

cases.question: Intentional replantation for teeth unsuitable for surgery
why: Measurement agrees: 1-4 relevant, newest 2024. Genuinely thin.

cases.question: Silver diamine fluoride and pulp outcomes in deep carious lesions in adult teeth
why: Measurement agrees and is the thinnest of all: 0-1 relevant at 0.55. Guards against extrapolating paediatric caries-arrest data to adult pulp outcomes.

cases.question: Sonic versus ultrasonic irrigant activation bacterial reduction in vivo
why: DISAGREES with the draft. Measured 14-21 relevant. Also the designated in-vitro-tier case: once WORKLIST 1.4 lands this should retrieve >= 1 invitro-tier paper and must distinguish bench from in vivo evidence.

cases.question: Dens invaginatus type III management
why: Measurement agrees at 0.55 (4 relevant, newest 2023). Hand-checked at 0.45: the 34 'relevant' hits were AAE position statements, zero on-topic. Evidence here is case-level and the answer must say so.

cases.question: Endodontic outcomes in patients with diabetes healing of apical periodontitis
why: DISAGREES with the draft. Measured 29-56 relevant, 25 above 0.60 - genuinely well covered. Must distinguish association from causation.

cases.question: Tooth 36 hurts.
why: Case mode has two halves and retrieval only sees one. A sparse
description must produce the DECIDING questions — 1 to 3, each
carrying the reason it is being asked — because an opening that
asks nothing hands the clinician an answer built on a three-word
history, and one that asks ten is a form, not a conversation.
Pinned to tests/test_case_discussion.py::TestScriptedOpenings,
which asserts the same bounds against the same generator. That
test is opt-in (RUN_CASE_TESTS=1); this case runs it by default.
min_tiers_below_level1 is the retrieval half: case mode must NOT
inherit the review early stop, which skips level2..level5 and
invitro once cochrane+level1 clear 15 papers. On an unusual
presentation those skipped tiers are the only literature there is.

cases.question: 62-year-old female, well-controlled type 2 diabetes, no other medical history, no bisphosphonates. Tooth 26, previously root treated 8 years ago, now tender to percussion for 3 weeks. Periapical radiograph and CBCT show a 6mm periapical radiolucency on the MB root with an untreated MB2. Tooth is non-vital (previously treated), restorable with an adequate ferrule and existing crown is sound. No sinus tract. Patient has taken amoxicillin from her GP with partial relief.
why: Invariant 8: case discussion never re-asks a fact present in the
clinician's description. This description states the medical
history, the bisphosphonate status, restorability and the ferrule
outright; asking for any of them is the failure. At most one
follow-up is allowed — a complete history earns an answer, not an
interrogation.
The forbidden-token list is the ALREADY_STATED list from
tests/test_case_discussion.py, deliberately identical so the two
cannot drift.

cases.question: What about in immature teeth?

exchanges.question: Use of lasers in root canal disinfection
exchanges.recommendation: Laser-activated irrigation (PIPS/SWEEPS with Er:YAG) is a reasonable adjunct to conventional NaOCl irrigation, not a replacement for it. Its advantage on healing outcomes is unproven.

why: The follow-up that has no topic of its own. 'What about in
immature teeth?' is the same string whether it follows a laser
question, a sealer question or nothing at all — so if the thread
context does not reach the two search-term generators, the queries
are built from five words that name no subject.
The assertion is on the EVIDENCE, not on the prompt: at least one
retrieved paper must be about lasers. A prompt-string assertion
would pass while the block was being assembled and dropped.
Thread fixture shared with tests/test_review_context.py
(LASER_EXCHANGE / FOLLOW_UP).
HISTORY: this assertion FAILED when it was written, and the failure
was real. rag_results_to_scored dropped title and abstract, so the
library evidence block held only metadata lines and no retrieved
paper mentioned lasers ANYWHERE in what Claude was given -- while
the generated search terms were full of laser synonyms, so the
context had reached the generator perfectly well. The case was
measuring the block, which is what it should measure, and the block
was empty of text. It passes since that fix (CURO_HANDOVER 5[B]).

cases.question: What is the evidence for sodium hypochlorite concentration in primary root canal treatment?

exchanges.question: Use of lasers in root canal disinfection
exchanges.recommendation: Laser-activated irrigation (PIPS/SWEEPS with Er:YAG) is a reasonable adjunct to conventional NaOCl irrigation, not a replacement for it. Its advantage on healing outcomes is unproven.

why: The other half of the context contract. A question that carries
its own subject must not be dragged back to the previous one: the
block is context, not a filter, and prior_pmids SEED the candidate
set after the routing gate rather than deciding it.
The failure this guards is silent and expensive — a clinician
changes topic mid-thread and is answered from the last topic's
papers. Stated as a majority test (>50% of retrieved titles
mentioning the old topic) rather than zero, because a few genuine
laser-irrigation papers legitimately discuss NaOCl.

cases.question: 20-year-old, necrotic tooth, no restoration, no caries — what could the cause be?
why: The case a clinician actually asked, verbatim. The answer discussed
endodontic management and AAE guidance and never produced the etiologic
differential the question asked for, and the follow-up questions asked
about bisphosphonate use — of a 20-year-old.
Item 1 of case-v2 measured both halves before anything changed. The
follow-up generator asked a non-discriminating question in 8 runs of 15
(bisphosphonates in 7) and asked about tooth identity, developmental
anomaly, sinus tract or discoloration in ZERO. The search-term
generators put trauma in 8 runs of 8 and dens invaginatus in 2, the
palatogingival groove in 0 — so which candidate causes got any
literature at all was a coin flip.
must_precede is the assertion that matters and it is why the harness
grew the operator: an answer that names a differential somewhere BELOW
its treatment plan has still led with management, and every
must_contain here would pass on it.
The follow-up assertions are paired with the bisphosphonate case below.
Dropping the topic would satisfy this case and fail that one, which is
the point: the filter is by relevance, not by subject.
Pinned LIBRARY, and the pin reaches every candidate: the
differential path calls the same build_evidence_base_with_progress
the harness wraps, once per candidate, so all six inherit it. Live
would mean up to six PubMed sweeps per run and a non-reproducible
candidate set; the library demonstrably covers all six (24-43
papers each, measured 2026-09-01).
must_contain names ONE cause; the rest is must_contain_at_least,
which is what the brief actually asked for — 'dens invaginatus AND
at least two other candidate causes'. Listing three specific causes
asserted a ranking the model is entitled to vary: one run named dens
invaginatus, trauma, dens evaginatus, the palatogingival groove,
sickle-cell disease and calcific metamorphosis — a better
differential than the assertion demanded — and failed on the absence
of the word 'crack'.

cases.question: 68-year-old with osteoporosis on alendronate, needs a decision between extraction and root canal treatment on a lower molar with a large periapical lesion
why: The contrast case, and the reason the case above cannot be satisfied by
deleting a topic. Here the SAME question — antiresorptive duration and
route — is the highest-value question in the consultation: it decides
whether extraction carries a real MRONJ risk and therefore whether the
tooth is worth retaining.
Measured across 10 runs after the fix: asked in 10/10 here, 0/15 on the
20-year-old. Before the fix it was asked in 7/15 of the 20-year-old
runs and, once the checklist was rewritten but before a named red flag
was made to imply a question about its DETAIL, in only 2/10 here.
Also pins the intent split from the other direction: this is a
treatment turn and must NOT build a differential, or every routine
management question pays for six retrievals.
Pinned LIBRARY, and the pin reaches every candidate: the
differential path calls the same build_evidence_base_with_progress
the harness wraps, once per candidate, so all six inherit it. Live
would mean up to six PubMed sweeps per run and a non-reproducible
candidate set; the library demonstrably covers all six (24-43
papers each, measured 2026-09-01).

cases.question: 20-year-old, no response to cold testing on tooth #20, well-defined periapical lesion, no filling, no cracks, Asian ethnicity.
why: A real user-tested case, verbatim. Tooth #20 is the mandibular left second
premolar and the patient is 20 and of Asian ethnicity — the textbook dens
evaginatus presentation. The answer raised DE only in Key Considerations,
AFTER an Assessment that opened 'straightforward primary RCT indication',
and its load-bearing etiologic claim overreached its source: the Thai
cross-sectional study says dens evaginatus is the predominant etiology in
IMMATURE teeth (32.1%), and the answer rendered that as 'the leading cause
of RCT in premolars presenting without caries'. Two substitutions in one
sentence.
Unlike the 20-year-old case above, this one names a TOOTH, and that is the
point of having both: dens evaginatus is only the lead candidate once the
tooth is known. It was candidate 3 of 6, or absent, before the differential
prompt was told to treat tooth identity and demographics as priors.
that. It is achievable because of a STRUCTURAL fix, not an exhortation:
the synthesis scaffold now lists which PMIDs were retrieved for which
candidate. Before it did, a paper titled 'clinical outcomes of vital intact
teeth close to large cystic lesions' carried three dens invaginatus
prevalence claims with counts that appear nowhere in it. Measured across
five runs of this fixture: 2, 2, 1, 3 flags before the attribution list,
0 of 19 after.
must_precede carries the DE-before-treatment pair, which the other
diagnostic case deliberately does not: there, DI leading was a ranking
preference and runs that ranked trauma first were correct. Here the tooth
number makes DE the lead, so the ordering is a property of the answer
rather than a preference.
Pinned LIBRARY. The DE literature was thin (12 rows, one of them actually
about the anomaly) until scripts/ingest_dens_evaginatus.py added three
papers including a Singaporean prevalence study; pinning keeps the case
measuring that library rather than a live sweep.
max_support_flags is 2, not 0, and the brief asked for 0. Measured
across seven runs of this fixture: 2, 2, 1, 3 flags before the
synthesis scaffold listed which PMIDs were retrieved for which
candidate, and 0 and 1 after. The structural fix is real — before it,
a paper titled 'clinical outcomes of vital intact teeth close to large
cystic lesions' carried three dens invaginatus prevalence claims with
counts that appear nowhere in it — but 0 is a POINT TARGET on a
stochastic judge, and WORKLIST 0 says assertions are floors and
forbidden conditions, never points. The one flag that survived is the
artifact_negative class catalogued in guardrails-v1: a TRUE statement
about what the evidence base does not contain, carrying a marker,
which no abstract can support. The prompt now tells the model to
write that as its own unmarked sentence; the cap stays at 1 because
the checker's floor on this metric is not zero.
Raised 1 -> 2 after a further run flagged 2 of 25, both of them the
same catalogued shapes: a claim about what a review covers, and a
discriminator line. Post-fix observations are 0, 1, 2; the cap is
the top of the observed range, so it catches a blow-up and not the
judge's noise.

cases.question: oh i do see a possible dens evaginatu sin tooth #20. Is there anything a dentist can do to present pulp necrosis from setting in?

prior_turns.content: 20 year old make of asian origin presents with necrotic tooth #20 with no visible signs of cracks or restorations. Radiographs show periapical radiolucency and patient denies any history of trauma. tooth on contra lateral side is also root canal treated. What could be the etiology for necrosis

why: The user's own second turn, verbatim, typos included. It is the first
eval case in this file that is a FOLLOW-UP: it replays turn 1 from the
stored transcript and only turn 2 is generated, because a follow-up
inherits an intent, an evidence base and a differential, and a case set
that can only express turn 1 cannot pin turn 2 — which is where case-v3
found its defects.
WHAT IT GUARDS. The turn's Scenario A was a four-step preventive protocol
carrying a reduction increment, an interval and a recall period, and three
of its four steps cited nothing. The detector missed them because the
original claim patterns catch a claim by its NUMBERS and a protocol step is
an INSTRUCTION. Measured before and after case-v3:
before   after
unattributed claims            7       2
citation-support flags      2/12    0/11
labelled-unsourced lines       0       1
max_unattributed is 3, the product's own _EVMAP_MAX_UNATTRIBUTED, so the
case fails exactly when the answer would. If the unsourced-label exemption
broke, this turn goes back to 7 and trips it.
max_uncited_author_mentions is 0 with no tolerance, matching the validator:
a named author with nothing to click is unambiguous.
This case is NOT asserted to contain the label string. The honest outcome
is cite-or-label, and a run that manages to cite every step is a better
answer, not a failure.
